the crowded aqueous media of living organisms are less favorable to the solvation of hydrophobically solvated solutes than the pure aqueous media.
the crowdedness of the media, in this case induced by trehalose, affects the solubility and the enthalpy, entropy and heat capacity of the solution of alcohals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the enthalpic and entropic effects that drive the solubilization of a given solute in a crowded solution are not additive, and the resulting change in Gibbs energy of solvation will depend on the solute’s chemical structure.
in crowded media, the enthalpy and entropy of solvation of a solute are not independent, but they are interrelated.
in crowded media, the hydrophobic effect is reduced, and the hydrophilic effect is increased.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in a crowded solution the solubility and the enthalpy and entropy of solution are inter-related and that the enthalpy term can be used as a proxy to predict changes in solubility.

the crowdedness of the intracellular media, which is a result of high protein concentration, will affect the solubility, and therefore the activity, of the solutes present in the media, in a way that will depend on the hydrophobic character of the solutes.
the thermodynamic parameters of the solution process are strongly affected by the crowding media and the hydrophobicity of the solute.
